item.title: Extreme weather, harmful chemicals escalating health risks among food workers, finds global report
item.description: Many farmworkers lack basic protection from extreme weather, including access to shade, rest breaks and drinking water, the report notes, adding that international labour standards are often ignored, while weak enforcement leaves workers exposed to dangerous conditions

item.title: Cotton prices surge ₹4,000 a candy, T.N. textile mills fret over costs
On paddy field conservation in Keralam
item.description: Neglecting paddy fields as a socio-ecological system that regulates local biodiversity, the hydrological cycle, and microclimate constitutes a grave failure, amid rising food insecurity and floods

item.title: All stakeholders must work together to resolve sugarcane growers’ issues: Karnataka CM D. K. Shivakumar
item.description: CM says meeting with farmers, sugar factory owners and government representatives will be convened; Ministers asked to prepare for local body polls

item.title: Maharashtra drought: Farmer sends money order of ₹5,000 to CM over ‘paltry’ interim aid by govt.
item.description: “I cultivated a soybean crop on 1.5 acres of my farm. I spent ₹25,000 and received a 60-kg yield. I could earn just ₹3,900. I borrowed ₹1,100 from my friend to send the money order,” Mr. Shaikh told reporters outside Surdi post office.

item.title: Land shortage cripples Agriculture Ministry’s weather network rollout
item.description: Project is a year behind deadline, with over 96% of planned rain gauges and weather stations yet to be installed; private partners say IMD is retrospectively insisting that sensors be installed on the ground, not on rooftops

item.title: Araku Pinery: New experiences at the community-led eco-tourism retreat
item.description: With pottery, camping, adventure rides and seasonal farms joining its pine-lined attractions, Araku Pinery is preparing for a busy tourist season

item.title: Rice millers fear steep hike in rice prices
Multiple factors to determine cotton crop for 2026-27
Cabinet approves hike in Rabi minimum support prices for 2027-28 season
item.description: The MSP for safflower was increased the most, by ₹675 per quintal to ₹7,215 per quintal, an increase of 10.3% over its level in the previous year

item.title: U.P. focuses on utilisation of Gram Sabha ponds, reservoirs, rivers to make fisheries backbone of rural livelihood
item.description: The State government says more than 80,000 hectares of Gram Sabha ponds and 2,205 km of rivers have been brought under leasing, and fish production has risen from 6.29 lakh tonnes to 15.90 lakh tonnes in eight years

item.title: Why Rayalaseema farmers fear a bumper crop more than drought; can the ₹1-lakh-crore horticulture hub change that?
item.description: Farmers in the region fear a bumper yield the most, because the lack of cold storage and market linkages and exploitation by middlemen often force them into distress sales

item.title: AIKMS calls for united movement against corporatisation of agriculture
How the science Nikolai Vavilov built changed how we save crops
item.description: One of Vavilov’s major contributions was a paper he published in 1926: even today, a century later, it remains the foundation of the study and use of crops and livestock
